edits.headline: Lindsay Clancy jury ends sixth day of deliberations without a verdict
edits.subheadline: One juror appeared to disagree with the other 11 in the Massachusetts murder trial, WBUR reported.
editorialBody: Jurors in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy ended a sixth day of deliberations in Plymouth, Massachusetts, on 3 September without a verdict, WBUR reported. Clancy is charged with killing her three young children. Her defence argues she had postpartum psychosis and is not criminally responsible.

One juror appeared to disagree with the other 11, according to WBUR. Judge William Sullivan repeated his explanation of reasonable doubt and declined a defence request to remove the juror. Jurors were due back on Friday.
ABC News aired a programme titled "I'm Not Ok: America's Postpartum Crisis".

Vice President JD Vance said the US was investigating a reported strike on a wedding in Kuhestak, southern Iran, and that he was "extremely skeptical" of the reports, Stars and Stripes reported. Iranian officials said at least five people were killed and nearly 70 wounded.
Flash floods in Nepal and China left hundreds dead and thousands missing, NPR reported.
Former NFL quarterback Mark Sanchez agreed to plead guilty over an October 2025 fight in Indianapolis in which he was stabbed, ProFootballTalk reported. A judge must still accept the plea.
A shooting at a downtown Minneapolis apartment building on 2 September left three people dead, including the suspect, and five wounded, the Associated Press reported.
